title: Short Stuff: Pimento Cheese!
summary: Short Stuff episode on pimento cheese. Josh and Chuck trace its origins: a late-1800s/early-1900s New York version made with cream cheese, mustard and chives, mass-produced and tinned for soldiers in World War One and popular from the 1920s to 1940s. The South reworked it: Griffin, Georgia became the pimento capital after getting pimento seeds from the Spanish consulate in the early 1900s, and Southern cooks swapped cream cheese for mayonnaise and used shredded cheddar. They compare it to deviled chicken spread, discuss family recipes, and mention the Masters' pimento cheese sandwich, whose longtime maker Nick Rangos took his recipe to the grave before caterer Wife Saver took over. The hosts also talk about Palmetto cheese, a gift from a listener, and serving pimento cheese cold or on a hot cheeseburger.
topics: New York cream cheese pimento cheese

segments.title: Opening banter and pimento spelling
segments.summary: Josh opens the Short Stuff episode with banter about the spelling of pimiento and introduces pimento cheese as a Southern favorite.

segments.title: Original New York pimento cheese
segments.summary: The hosts explain that pimento cheese began in New York around World War One as a mix of pimentos, cream cheese, mustard and chives, which was tinned and popular with soldiers and Americans through the 1920s to 1940s. Josh and Chuck also discuss mustard preferences, including Coleman's.
topics: New York cream cheese pimento cheese

segments.title: Pimento peppers arrive from Spain
segments.summary: Pimento peppers came from Spain to America in the late 1800s and were mild and colorful. Cream cheese was new at that time, and mass-produced pimento spreads and sandwiches spread through cookbooks and grocery stores.

segments.title: Griffin, Georgia and the Southern transformation
segments.summary: The South changed pimento cheese by dropping cream cheese and mustard. Griffin, Georgia became the pimento capital after getting seeds from the Spanish consulate in the early 1900s and harvesting pimentos by 1916.

segments.title: Deviled chicken spread comparison
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh compare the original pimento spread to deviled chicken spread, a salty, whipped chicken spread sold in Southern convenience stores next to Vienna sausage.

segments.title: Mayonnaise and cheddar replace cream cheese
segments.summary: Southern cooks replaced cream cheese with mayonnaise and added shredded cheddar, leaving pimentos, mayonnaise and cheese as the core ingredients. Family recipes vary in spices, cheese and extras such as bacon or jalapenos.

segments.title: Palmetto cheese, the Masters and Augusta
segments.summary: The hosts mention Palmetto cheese, a listener gift from Queen Charlotte. They then discuss the Masters pimento cheese sandwich at Augusta National, whose maker Nick Rangos kept his recipe secret until his death, and whose new caterer Wife Saver also keeps its recipe secret.

segments.title: Serving pimento cheese cold or hot
segments.summary: Pimento cheese is usually served cold on crackers or in sandwiches, and it is also good on a hot cheeseburger. The hosts say heating it changes the flavor.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wrap up the short episode and sign off.
